text:
Ana R: Heads-up — I ran the onboarding eval for hailstone-embed-v1 (int8 per-tensor) on the multilang holdout. Quick thread with numbers and next steps.
Miles: Nice, drop the results pls :eyes:
Ana R: Summary first: baseline (float16) recall@10=0.872, int8 per-tensor recall@10=0.821 (5.9% relative drop). Silhouette down from 0.42 -> 0.33. Precision@1 also down ~4%.
Devon: ouch. which dataset?
Ana R: Multilang-anchored-100k (mix en, es, fr, de). Held out 10k queries.
Samir: Any sign it's a calibration shift vs representational collapse? e.g., norm distributions?
Ana R: Good question. I plotted L2 norms and cosine distributions. Means are similar but variance increased a bit for int8. Attached snippet: 
```
# quant eval summary
model: hailstone-embed-v1
quant: int8_per_tensor
nq:10000
recall@1  r@1_f16:0.792 r@1_int8:0.762
recall@10 r@10_f16:0.872 r@10_int8:0.821
silhouette f16:0.42 int8:0.33
```
Miles: Did you run per-channel int8? that often helps for heterogeneous weights.
Ana R: Not yet — only per-tensor and a quick int4 simulation. Per-channel queued next.
Devon: Any failures in the quant pipeline (outliers/clipping)? logs?
Ana R: No clipping warnings. Quantizer histograms show long tail on a small subset of embedding layer weights (top 2% of dims). Could be low-level sensitivity.
Samir: Also worth checking top-k neighbor shifts for high-confidence queries vs noisy queries. If only noisy ones change, impact might be smaller in prod.
Ana R: I did stratified recall: for high-sim queries (f16 cosine>0.8) recall@1 drop is 1.2% absolute. For mid-sim (0.5-0.8) drop is 6.8% absolute. So mid-range suffers most.
Devon: That suggests quant noise around decision boundary. Maybe try bias-correction or small-scale distillation.
Miles: Can you run batch size sensitivity? I know inference kernel differences sometimes affect KV cache/order but for embed offline it might be quantization math differences at scale.
Ana R: Ran microbatch x2,x8 no change. This is pure quant error in weights.
Samir: Proposed next steps: 1) per-channel int8 run 2) ran per-channel with symmetric vs asymmetric 3) try 8-bit quant with layerwise minmax vs percentile clipping (99.9th) 4) run kNN recall only on anchor-heavy queries 5) try tiny distill on 1M examples to smooth boundaries. Anyone object?
Miles: +1 do per-channel and percentile clipping. Also run cluster compactness metrics (DB index) and nearest neighbor rank flip counts.
Ana R: On it. Scheduling jobs now. Using eval script: `python eval/embeddings_eval.py --model hailstone-embed-v1 --quant per_channel_int8 --dataset multilang-anchored-100k --out hailstone_int8_pc.json`
ops-bot: buildkite: started pipeline emb-eval/hailstone-int8-perchannel (#5872)
eval-bot: quick metric summary will post when job finishes.
Devon: FYI — if per-channel fixes most, consider shipping per-channel quant profile in dedicated and hosted but keep float fallback for Private. We'll need to record model/resource tradeoff in the catalog doc.
Ana R: Agreed. I'll also run a small re-eval with 50k synthetic noisy queries to estimate user-perceptible regressions.
Samir: If per-channel doesn't close gap, try quant-aware fine-tuning for 1 epoch at lr 1e-5 on contrastive anchor set. Past success on similar models.
Miles: Great plan. Can you drop the result artifacts to s3 and ping here? path convention: s3://redwood-embeds/onboard/hailstone/v1/int8_perchannel/{run_ts}/metrics.json
Ana R: Will do. ETA ~45m for per-channel run.
Miles: Thanks — let's reconvene after metrics. :thumbsup:
